model_answer: **(A)** For DC $\omega=0$, so $X_C$ is infinite; for AC $X_C$ is finite and falls as frequency rises.

stem: Define power factor. Under what condition is the current in an AC circuit wattless? Give one example.
model_answer:
Power factor $\cos\phi=\dfrac{\text{true power}}{\text{apparent power}}=\dfrac{R}{Z}$, where φ is the phase difference between V and I. [1]
Wattless when $\phi=90^\circ$ ($\cos\phi=0$): e.g. a purely inductive or purely capacitive circuit; average power $VI\cos\phi=0$. [1]

stem: Describe the working of an AC generator with a labelled diagram and show that the emf induced in it is $\varepsilon=NBA\omega\sin\omega t$.
model_answer:
Labelled diagram: coil (armature) between the poles of a magnet, axle, slip rings, carbon brushes, external load. [1]
Coil of $N$ turns, area $A$, turned at ω in field B; at time $t$ the normal makes $\theta=\omega t$ with B, so $\Phi=NBA\cos\omega t$. [1]
$\varepsilon=-\dfrac{d\Phi}{dt}=\boxed{NBA\omega\sin\omega t}$; peak $NBA\omega$ when the plane of the coil is parallel to B. [1]

label: PYQ-style
stem:
(a) Explain the principle and working of a transformer with a labelled diagram. For an ideal transformer, show that $\dfrac{V_s}{V_p}=\dfrac{N_s}{N_p}=\dfrac{I_p}{I_s}$. [3]
(b) Name two causes of energy loss in a real transformer and say how each is reduced. [2]
model_answer:
(a) Labelled diagram: primary and secondary coils on a laminated soft-iron core. Principle: mutual induction. [1]
The same flux Φ links every turn: $\varepsilon_p=-N_p\dfrac{d\Phi}{dt}$, $\varepsilon_s=-N_s\dfrac{d\Phi}{dt}$, so $\dfrac{V_s}{V_p}=\dfrac{N_s}{N_p}$. [1]
Ideal (no loss): $V_pI_p=V_sI_s$, so $\dfrac{I_p}{I_s}=\dfrac{V_s}{V_p}=\dfrac{N_s}{N_p}$. [1]
(b) Eddy currents in the core: reduced by a laminated core. [1]
Copper ($I^2R$) loss in the windings: reduced by thick copper wire. (Also accept: flux leakage, coils wound over each other; hysteresis, soft-iron core.) [1]

scheme.step: (a) Labelled diagram: primary and secondary coils on a laminated soft-iron core. Principle: mutual induction.

(b) Eddy currents in the core: reduced by a laminated core.
Copper ($I^2R$) loss in the windings: reduced by thick copper wire. (Also accept: flux leakage, coils wound over each other; hysteresis, soft-iron core.)

label: PYQ-style
stem: In a series LCR circuit a resistance of 30 Ω, an inductive reactance of 100 Ω and a capacitive reactance of 40 Ω are connected to an AC source. Find (i) the impedance and (ii) the phase angle between the voltage and the current.
hint: Find the net reactance X_L − X_C first, then Z = √(R² + X²) and tan φ = X/R.
model_answer:
*How much to write: 4–5 lines · 3 minutes* **Given:** $R=30\ \Omega$, $X_L=100\ \Omega$, $X_C=40\ \Omega$
**To find:** $Z$ and $\phi$ $$\begin{aligned}Z&=\sqrt{R^2+(X_L-X_C)^2}\\&=\sqrt{30^2+60^2}=\sqrt{4500}\end{aligned}$$ $$\boxed{Z=67.1\ \Omega}$$ $$\begin{aligned}\tan\phi&=\frac{X_L-X_C}{R}\\&=\frac{60}{30}=2\end{aligned}$$ $$\boxed{\phi=63.4^\circ}$$ Since $X_L>X_C$, the voltage leads the current: the circuit is inductive. :::tip Your answer must contain - the net reactance $X_L-X_C$ found first - $Z=\sqrt{R^2+(X_L-X_C)^2}$ with the values substituted - the phase angle from $\tan\phi$, with the lead or lag stated ::: **Marks are lost for:** adding $X_L+X_C$; leaving out the phase angle's lead or lag; giving Z in terms of R only.
